title: Prostate Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for prostate cancer. Branches by disease state (localized/regional; biochemical recurrence; non-metastatic castration-resistant (nmCRPC/M0); metastatic castration-sensitive (mCSPC); metastatic castration-resistant (mCRPC)), then by localized risk group, metastatic volume, and mCRPC biomarker/burden (HRR/BRCA, MSI-H/dMMR, PSMA-positive, bone-predominant). Each option ROUTES to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; modality-only options with no dose protocol (active surveillance, radium-223, tissue-agnostic pembrolizumab, surgery/radiation) are shown as guidance only with NO dose. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion; the physician selects and the existing dose engine computes patient doses. Risk-group and metastatic-volume stratification are standard oncology constructs; structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate Cancer, no proprietary content reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer. Options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers.

nodes.name: Disease state
nodes.title: Disease state
nodes.description: Prostate cancer therapy is defined first by disease state. Choose the current clinical state.

nodes.name: Localized risk group
nodes.title: Localized: risk group
nodes.description: Stratify localized/regional disease by risk group (PSA, ISUP grade group / Gleason, clinical T stage, and % positive cores). Risk group drives whether systemic therapy is added to local therapy.

nodes.name: mCSPC volume
nodes.title: mCSPC: metastatic burden
nodes.description: In metastatic castration-sensitive disease, metastatic volume (e.g. visceral disease and/or four or more bone metastases with at least one beyond the vertebral column/pelvis) and de-novo vs recurrent presentation guide the intensity of androgen-deprivation intensification.

nodes.name: mCRPC option
nodes.title: mCRPC: biomarker / burden
nodes.description: In mCRPC, select the directing feature. Obtain germline + somatic HRR testing, MMR/MSI (or TMB), and PSMA-PET where available. Prior therapy also guides sequencing (an ARPI-first patient who progresses is typically offered a taxane, and vice-versa).

nodes.name: Active surveillance
nodes.title: Very-low / low risk: active surveillance
nodes.description: Very-low and low-risk localized disease is generally managed with active surveillance (serial PSA, DRE, and repeat biopsy/imaging), with definitive local therapy (radical prostatectomy or radiation) reserved for reclassification. No systemic therapy; monitoring only. Physician decides.

nodes.name: Favorable intermediate
nodes.title: Favorable intermediate: local therapy
nodes.description: Favorable-intermediate-risk disease: radiation (EBRT or brachytherapy) or radical prostatectomy; active surveillance remains an option for selected patients. Short-course ADT is generally NOT required. If ADT is used with radiation, the ADT regimen is referenced below; radiation/surgery are procedures the physician arranges.

nodes.name: Unfavorable intermediate
nodes.title: Unfavorable intermediate: RT + short-term ADT
nodes.description: Unfavorable-intermediate-risk disease: radiation with short-term (about 4-6 months) androgen-deprivation therapy, or radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection. ADT regimen referenced below; physician selects and arranges local therapy.

nodes.name: High / very-high risk
nodes.title: High / very-high risk: RT + long-term ADT (+/- abiraterone)
nodes.description: High- and very-high-risk (and node-positive) disease: radiation with long-term (about 18-36 months) androgen-deprivation therapy, with abiraterone added for selected very-high-risk/regional disease; or radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection in appropriate candidates. ADT and abiraterone regimens referenced below.

nodes.name: Biochemical recurrence
nodes.title: Biochemical recurrence: restage + salvage
nodes.description: Rising PSA after prior local therapy: restage (PSMA-PET where available) to distinguish local vs regional vs distant recurrence. Options: salvage radiation with or without ADT (after prostatectomy), salvage local therapy (after primary radiation), or observation when PSA doubling-time is long. ADT regimen referenced below; physician selects.

nodes.name: nmCRPC
nodes.title: nmCRPC (M0 CRPC): continue ADT + next-generation ARPI
nodes.description: Non-metastatic castration-resistant disease with a short PSA doubling-time (about 10 months or less): continue androgen-deprivation and add a next-generation androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (apalutamide, darolutamide, or enzalutamide) to delay metastasis. Apalutamide/darolutamide are the same class as the enzalutamide regimen referenced below; physician selects the agent.

nodes.name: mCSPC doublet
nodes.title: mCSPC (low-volume): ADT + ARPI doublet
nodes.description: Metastatic castration-sensitive, low-volume: androgen-deprivation therapy intensified with an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone, apalutamide, or enzalutamide). ADT alone is no longer preferred. Physician selects the ARPI.

nodes.name: mCSPC triplet
nodes.title: mCSPC (high-volume): ADT + docetaxel + ARPI (triplet)
nodes.description: Metastatic castration-sensitive, high-volume/de-novo: triplet therapy - androgen-deprivation plus docetaxel plus an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone or darolutamide) for fit patients; ADT + ARPI doublet is an alternative. Component regimens referenced below.

nodes.name: mCRPC standard
nodes.title: mCRPC: standard ARPI / taxane
nodes.description: mCRPC with no actionable biomarker: an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone or enzalutamide) if not previously used, or taxane chemotherapy (docetaxel, then cabazitaxel on progression). Avoid sequential ARPI-to-ARPI where possible. Physician selects.

nodes.name: mCRPC PARP
nodes.title: mCRPC, HRR / BRCA: PARP inhibitor
nodes.description: mCRPC with a homologous-recombination-repair (HRR) or BRCA1/2 alteration: a PARP inhibitor (olaparib), typically after or combined with an ARPI. Physician selects.

nodes.name: mCRPC immunotherapy
nodes.title: mCRPC, MSI-H / dMMR: immunotherapy
nodes.description: mCRPC that is microsatellite-instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch-repair-deficient (dMMR): pembrolizumab under the tissue-agnostic indication. No prostate-specific dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet, so this is shown as guidance only - the physician arranges the tissue-agnostic pembrolizumab regimen. Guidance only; no dose computed here.

nodes.name: mCRPC radioligand
nodes.title: mCRPC, PSMA-positive: radioligand therapy
nodes.description: mCRPC with PSMA-positive imaging (and typically after an ARPI and a taxane): Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy. Physician selects.

nodes.name: mCRPC radium-223
nodes.title: mCRPC, bone-predominant: radium-223
nodes.description: mCRPC with symptomatic bone metastases and no visceral disease: radium-223 (an alpha-emitter) prolongs survival and reduces symptomatic skeletal events; not combined with abiraterone/prednisone. No dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet, so this is shown as guidance only - the physician arranges the regimen. Guidance only; no dose computed here.
